content:
The [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Count the digits in any number — integer part, decimal places and total. Enter your number and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Count the digits in any number: how many before the decimal point, how many after it, and the total. The sign is ignored, leading zeros do not count, and a trailing decimal point with nothing after it counts as zero decimal places. It is the quick way to check the length of an ID number, a result, or a value you are about to paste into a form with a digit limit. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Number of Digits Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your number. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste the number.
2. Read the digits before and after the decimal point, and the total.
3. Negative signs are ignored — only the digits themselves are counted.

## Formula

Total digits = digits in the integer part + digits in the fractional part. The sign and the decimal point itself are not digits.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 12345 has 5 digits, all before the decimal point. −12345.678 has 5 digits before the point, 3 after it, and 8 digits in total. 0.001 has 1 digit before the point and 3 after it. Try the same figures in the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Number: 12345), the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) returns Digits before the decimal point: 5, Digits after the decimal point: 0, Total digits: 5, Is an integer: Yes, Sign: Positive. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## What counts as a digit

Only the characters 0–9 count. The minus sign, the plus sign and the decimal point are not digits, and leading zeros in the integer part (007 is the number 7, with 1 digit) do not add to the count. Decimal places are counted exactly as written: 1.50 has 2 digits after the point, even though the trailing zero adds nothing to the value.

## Why count digits at all

Digit counts matter whenever a system limits them: credit-card numbers have 16 digits, a US phone number has 10, and many forms reject values that are too long. In programming, the digit count tells you the order of magnitude of a number — a 6-digit number is at least 100,000 — and in school maths it is the first step in rounding and significant-figure work.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Leading zeros do not count: 007 is a 1-digit number.
- The decimal point and the minus sign are never counted as digits.
- For very large numbers, use the digit count to check the order of magnitude at a glance.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many digits are in 12345?

Five — all before the decimal point. The total digit count is the integer-part digits plus the fractional-part digits. Try it with your own numbers in the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does the minus sign count as a digit?

No. Only 0–9 count as digits, so −12345.678 has 8 digits: 5 before the decimal point and 3 after it. Try it with your own numbers in the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do leading zeros count?

No. 007 is the number 7, so it has 1 digit. Trailing zeros after the decimal point do count, because they are written digits: 1.50 has 2 decimal places. Try it with your own numbers in the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Number of Digits Calculator use?

Total digits = digits in the integer part + digits in the fractional part. The sign and the decimal point itself are not digits. You can see it in action in the [Number of Digits Calculator](/number-of-digits) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
